clue.text: Confining him thus, law is retrograde, capricious

indicators.note: the reversed law closes around the other pieces, holding them in as if confined
retrograde means moving backwards, so the word law is read from its end

parts.note: taken as written
sic is Latin for thus, as printed after a quoted error

explanation.surface: Someone notes that keeping a man restrained by a backward law is erratic and arbitrary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Confining' puts HIM and SIC inside WAL, the word law turned round by 'is retrograde'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe behaviour driven by sudden fancies rather than reason.

clue.text: By implication may this man lose in defeat?

definitions.text: By implication may this man lose in defeat?

parts.words: By implication may this man lose in defeat?
parts.note: the superlative of bad implies the poorest man loses, and as a verb the word means to beat

explanation.surface: A question whether a man is implied to lose when beaten.
explanation.walkthrough: As a verb the word means to defeat; as a superlative it suggests the lowest-ranked competitor, the one likely to lose.
explanation.definitionFit: To get the better of someone in a fight, an old verb sense of beat.

clue.text: Nightmare in island republic almost overcoming us

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter of the island name is dropped

parts.note: Cuba is a Caribbean island republic
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bad dream about being in a Caribbean state that nearly overwhelms us.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims CUBA to CUB; 'overcoming' just puts IN and CUB above US in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: An incubus was a demon thought to lie on sleepers, so the word came to mean an oppressive bad dream.

clue.text: She acts with Tree, but so roguishly

indicators.note: roguishly suggests mischief, so the letters are knocked out of order

explanation.surface: An actress performs alongside the actor-manager Tree, though playfully.
explanation.walkthrough: Herbert Beerbohm Tree was a famous Victorian London actor-manager, which gives the surface its stage setting.
explanation.definitionFit: A soubrette is an actress playing a pert maid or coquette in comedy.

clue.text: Old friend a relative in the provision business?

parts.note: to cater is to supply food, the business of provisioning
a cousin is a relative

explanation.surface: A long-standing companion and kinsman who runs a catering firm.
explanation.walkthrough: An old word: Shakespeare uses it for close friends.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic term for an intimate companion, someone on familiar terms.

clue.text: Money I had placed under cover

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for a pound, from Latin libra
contracted, I had becomes I'd

explanation.surface: Someone kept cash hidden out of sight.
explanation.walkthrough: The held clue was cut to 'On'; the page prints it in full.
explanation.definitionFit: A top for a box or pot is something that closes it over.

clue.text: Rock-bound inlet needs crossing without one

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the crossing goes around one

parts.note: a ford is a shallow place for crossing a river
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A sea inlet among cliffs has to be crossed without anyone along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' here means outside, not lacking: FORD sits outside I.
explanation.definitionFit: A Norwegian-style inlet is a long narrow arm of sea between steep rock walls.

clue.text: A criminal, see, hiding, in the marshland

indicators.note: the marshland is hiding the other word by holding it within

parts.note: a fen is low marshy land, as in the Fens of eastern England
lo is an old word for see, as in lo and behold

explanation.surface: An outlaw is spotted lying low out in the marshes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hiding' puts LO inside FEN. The Fens are a marshy region of eastern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone convicted of a serious offence.

clue.text: Drawing this when on strike on the railway

parts.note: workers on strike are said to be out
a railway line

explanation.surface: A sketch of a railwayman during a stoppage.
explanation.definitionFit: A sketch showing just the shape or contour of something.

clue.text: Daisy's sadly without verve — indigestion?

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the shuffled letters go around the verve
sadly signals that the letters are in a sorry, disordered state

parts.note: pep is energy or verve

explanation.surface: Daisy has lost her energy, perhaps because of an upset stomach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly' rearranges DAISYS (the S of the possessive counts) into DYS...SIA, and 'without' puts it around PEP.
explanation.definitionFit: Dyspepsia is the medical word for an upset stomach after eating.

clue.text: Tell a tale as scrutineers may do

explanation.surface: A storyteller is likened to election officials checking ballots.
explanation.definitionFit: To narrate a story is to relate it in detail; officials checking a close vote count the ballots a second time.

clue.text: Enlarges various details

indicators.note: various suggests the letters of details taken in a varied order

explanation.surface: Something expands with assorted particulars added.
explanation.definitionFit: To widen or expand, as a pupil does in dim light.

clue.text: Raised row about Black River

indicators.note: the raised row is placed around the abbreviation, holding it inside

parts.note: a tier is one of a set of stepped rows of seats rising one above another
B is the pencil-grading abbreviation for black

explanation.surface: A stepped bank beside a dark river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raised' looks like a reversal signal but is part of the definition of TIER. The Tiber flows through Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tiber is the Italian watercourse on which Rome stands.

clue.text: Abstruse ceremonial about second decapitation

indicators.note: the ceremonial word is wrapped around the beheaded second

parts.note: a rite is a ceremonial act

indicators.note: decapitation cuts off the head, so the opening letter of the word second goes

parts.note: taken as written before losing its head

explanation.surface: An obscure ritual concerning a second beheading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'decapitation' removes S from SECOND, leaving ECOND, which goes inside RITE.
explanation.definitionFit: Recondite knowledge is obscure and hard to understand, known only to a few.

clue.text: Firm returned lyric — little money one concludes for the connoisseurs

indicators.note: the numeral comes at the end of the run

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the lyric word is read backwards

parts.note: a song is a lyric
a cent is a small coin
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A company sent back a song, and its small fee went to the experts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns SONG into GNOS; 'concludes' puts I last.
explanation.definitionFit: Experts with refined, discerning knowledge in a field such as art.

clue.text: A ship made by a fool

parts.note: SS stands for steamship, as in a ship's name prefix

explanation.surface: A vessel built by an idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: A donkey is proverbially stupid, so the word names a silly person.

clue.text: Sailors, on reform intent, are not indulging

parts.note: ABs are able seamen, ordinary sailors

indicators.note: reform means to reshape, so the letters of intent are rearranged

explanation.surface: Seamen who have resolved to mend their ways are going without drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on reform' rearranges INTENT into TINENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Refraining from pleasures, especially alcohol.

clue.text: Not minded to be inconsiderate?

explanation.surface: Someone without a thought is being uncaring.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally lacking any idea in one's head, and also careless of other people's feelings.

clue.text: Physician — the one who stole Belinda's lock?

parts.note: in Pope's The Rape of the Lock the Baron snips a curl from Belinda, rape there meaning seizure

explanation.surface: Asking whether the doctor is the person who took a lady's curl.
explanation.walkthrough: Pope's poem The Rape of the Lock uses rape in its old sense of carrying off; the Baron steals Belinda's hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A therapist treats illness, so is a kind of healer.

clue.text: Viewer not designed for cyclopean types

definitions.text: Viewer not designed for cyclopean types

parts.words: Viewer not designed for cyclopean types
parts.note: a viewing device using two eyes to see depth, useless to a one-eyed Cyclops

explanation.surface: A gadget unsuitable for one-eyed giants.
explanation.walkthrough: A Cyclops has a single eye; this viewer shows two pictures, one to each eye, to give a 3D effect.
explanation.definitionFit: The instrument gives each eye a slightly different picture so the brain perceives depth.

clue.text: Beethoven Symphony about the first of these blue books?

indicators.note: the symphony name goes around the single letter

parts.note: the Eroica is Beethoven's Third Symphony

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word these is taken

explanation.surface: A question whether a famous symphony relates to some racy literature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts T, from 'the first of these', inside EROICA. Blue here means indecent.
explanation.definitionFit: Erotic literature or art, with blue meaning smutty.

clue.text: Vegetable much like another sort of nut

explanation.surface: A green vegetable compared with a kind of nut.
explanation.walkthrough: Three senses: the vegetable; 'as like as two peas', for things much alike; and the pea in peanut.
explanation.definitionFit: The green pod seed is a vegetable, two of them proverbially look identical, and the groundnut takes its name in part from it.

clue.text: Left about ten? That's ominous

indicators.note: the side word is placed around the number

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone departed at around ten, a bad sign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts TEN inside PORT, between R and T.
explanation.definitionFit: An omen of something bad to come; the definition is a phrase for a thing that is a bad sign.

clue.text: Not a vital sort of chemistry

explanation.surface: A branch of chemistry is said to be unimportant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vital' is meant in its root sense of living: the chemistry of non-living substances.
explanation.definitionFit: Not arising from living organisms, and the name of the chemistry branch dealing with minerals and metals.

clue.text: Not enough of this penal diet for Oliver

definitions.text: Not enough of this penal diet for Oliver

parts.words: Not enough of this penal diet for Oliver
parts.note: Dickens's Oliver Twist asks for more of the thin workhouse porridge

explanation.surface: Oliver Twist found his workhouse ration too meagre.
explanation.walkthrough: In Oliver Twist the boy famously asks 'Please, sir, I want some more' of the workhouse porridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Thin oatmeal boiled in water, workhouse and prison fare.

clue.text: It gave Hamlet's "rat" an inadequate hiding

definitions.text: It gave Hamlet's "rat" an inadequate hiding

parts.words: It gave Hamlet's "rat" an inadequate hiding
parts.note: Polonius, called a rat by Hamlet, hid behind a wall hanging and was stabbed through it

explanation.surface: Something failed to conceal the eavesdropper Hamlet mistook for a rat.
explanation.walkthrough: In Shakespeare's play Hamlet cries 'a rat!' and stabs Polonius through the tapestry he hides behind.
explanation.definitionFit: A tapestry wall hanging, named after the French weaving town, like the one Polonius hid behind.

clue.text: Full title of the Comte de Buffon's man

explanation.surface: Someone seeks the full name of a French nobleman's servant.
explanation.walkthrough: Buffon said 'le style est l'homme même': the manner is the man himself.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal designation such as His Grace, and in Buffon's maxim a writer's manner of expression equals the person.

clue.text: Odyssey by river perhaps for a man of taste

parts.note: Homer's Odyssey is an example of an epic poem, as perhaps hints
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire, a crossword standby

explanation.surface: A long voyage along a river suits a connoisseur.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' marks the Odyssey as one example of an EPIC. The Ure is a river in Yorkshire, northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: A gourmet: someone with refined enjoyment of food and drink.

clue.text: Time for rubbing out when over sure

indicators.note: over here means finished with, so the word sure is done away with

parts.note: erasure is the act of rubbing out
taken as written

explanation.surface: It is time to stop erasing once confident.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when over' removes SURE from ERASURE.
explanation.definitionFit: An age or epoch, a period of history.

clue.text: Refusal to admit one surgeon shows artlessness

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so the refusal takes the other pieces inside it

parts.note: nay is an old word for no, a refusal
the Roman numeral for one is I
a vet is an animal surgeon

explanation.surface: A doctor's refusal to take a patient shows lack of guile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to admit' puts I and VET inside NAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Innocence and simplicity, a lack of worldly sophistication.

clue.text: He leaves the bird some scent

indicators.note: leaves means goes away from, so the word He is taken out

parts.note: the rail is a marsh bird
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man departs from the bird, leaving some odour behind.
explanation.walkthrough: THE RAIL less HE leaves TRAIL. 'He' looks like a person but is the letters taken out.
explanation.definitionFit: A hunting sense: the trail is the track of scent an animal leaves for hounds to follow.

clue.text: Philosopher in real trouble is taking small drink

indicators.note: the remaining pieces sit inside the troubled letters
trouble suggests the letters of real being disturbed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
a tot is a small measure of spirits

explanation.surface: A thinker in real difficulty is having a quick drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' turns REAL into ARLE; 'in' puts IS and TOT inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek thinker, pupil of Plato and tutor of Alexander the Great.
